newsitem.title: USA: USG spot methanol moves up a touch on Texas blast.
newsitem.headline: USG spot methanol moves up a touch on Texas blast.

text.p: Spot methanol prices in Houston moved up in an initial knee-jerk reaction to a blast Tuesday morning at the Hoechst Celanese methanol plant near Houston, but traders said they were taking a wait-and-see attitude.

The unit, run jointly by Hoechst Celanese, a unit of Germany's Hoechst AG, and by Valero Energy Corp, can produce nearly 13,000 barrels per day of methanol, much of which is used to produce the gasoline additive MTBE (methyl tertiary butyl ether).
Traders said spot prices had risen a cent to between 47 and 48 cents a gallon following the explosion.
"It could go up a few cents more if it's down for a while," said one MTBE trader, noting it was too early to know for sure how serious the blast was.

The blast occurred at 0700 CST/1300 GMT on Tuesday, a day after the plant, southeast of Houston in Clear Lake, Texas, was pulled off line. There were no injuries. An investigation into the blast is now underway, a plant official said.

Traders and industry sources said the facility was pulled off line due to a "heat exchanger" problem, contradicting earlier comments by a spokesman at the plant, who said the unit was taken out of service for planned maintenance.

Traders noted the key question at this point is how long the explosion will keep the plant idled, since the company had reportedly stockpiled enough product to last through five to seven days of work on the unit.
"The people who own product say (prices) will go up further, those who don't say they won't," the MTBE trader said.

Gasoline futures traders on the New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX) meanwhile said the blast may have helped to lift prices earlier Tuesday, but noted it remained a peripheral consideration at this point.
Gasoline futures on NYMEX have a deliverability specification calling for MTBE at about 11 percent by volume, and MTBE is about half methanol by volume.
-- Oliver Ludwig, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1633
